Portfolio Manager – European & Australian Securitized Products
(PGIM Credit - Securitized Products, London)
A GLOBAL LEADING ASSET MANAGER WITH A DIVERSE & INCLUSIVE CULTURE
As the Global Asset Management business of Prudential, we’re always looking for ways to improve financial services. We’re passionate about making a meaningful impact - touching the lives of millions and solving financial challenges in an ever-changing world.
We also believe talent is key to achieving our vision and are intentional about building a culture on respect and collaboration. When you join PGIM, you’ll unlock a motivating and impactful career – all while growing your skills and advancing your profession at one of the world’s leading global asset managers!
If you’re not afraid to think differently and challenge the status quo, come and be a part of a dedicated team that’s investing in your future by shaping tomorrow today.
At PGIM, You Can!
What you will do
We are seeking an experienced Portfolio Manager to join our Securitized Products group in London, with responsibility for investing in non-US securitized assets denominated in EUR, GBP and AUD. The successful candidate will be fully integrated within the global Securitized Products team and manage these investments within portfolios across European and Australian RMBS, ABS and CMBS on behalf of all third party and proprietary portfolios.  CLO experience is a plus, but not a requirement.
This is a senior, market-facing role. The Portfolio Manager will partner closely with the US-based sector portfolio managers, the Securitized Products research teams in London and the US, and the firm’s macroeconomic research professionals. The individual will serve as a primary point of contact in the London market for dealers, issuers, arrangers and other counterparties.
What you can expect
·       Actively manage and construct portfolios of EUR, GBP and AUD securitized assets across RMBS, consumer and commercial ABS and CMBS.
·       Responsibility for sub-sector ”sleeve” asset allocation, security selection, position sizing, capital structure positioning and trade execution within assigned risk budgets and client guidelines.
·       Generate and articulate relative value trade ideas across sectors, currencies, and capital structure, including cross-market comparisons against US securitized and corporate credit.
·       Source opportunities through buy-side and sell-side networks and direct-to-issuer relationships and use scale to negotiate favourable terms as an anchor investor.
·       Ensure compliance with applicable regulatory regimes, including UK/EU securitisation risk retention and due diligence requirements (Article 5/7), STS eligibility, and client-specific capital constraints.
·       Partner with the Securitized Products research team on ongoing surveillance of collateral performance, internal ratings and event-driven review of positions.
·       Actively contribute to the weekly desk head meetings and relative value forums that set investment strategy across the global Securitized Products platform.
·       Represent our Securitized Products capabilities with clients, consultants and prospects, contributing to portfolio reviews, RFPs, market commentary and conference participation.
·       Carry our team culture of high intellectual honesty and mutual respect with colleagues while always acting ethically, with conviction and great humility for the benefit of our clients.
·       As a senior leader, mentor and develop junior investment professionals in London.
What you will bring
·       BA/BS degree required; MBA, MS and/or CFA are preferred.
·       Significant years of investment experience in securitized products at an asset manager, insurance company, bank or hedge fund, with a demonstrable track record of portfolio management or risk-taking.
·       Deep expertise across European securitized markets (UK, Dutch, Irish, Spanish, Italian and pan-European RMBS/ABS/CMBS) with direct experience in AUD-denominated securitizations strongly preferred.
·       Command of UK and EU securitisation regulation, Solvency II / Solvency UK treatment, and the ability to navigate insurance capital, accounting and rating considerations across jurisdictions.
·       Established relationships across dealers, issuers, originators, servicers and arrangers in Europe and Australia.
·       Ability to review and interpret legal documentation, including offering circulars, servicing agreements and intercreditor arrangements.
·       Excellent written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to present investment recommendations to investment committees, clients and consultants.
·       Highly organised, detail-oriented and able to manage multiple priorities across time zones in a collaborative, globally integrated team.
What will set you apart?
·       Candidates who have completed internships and/or have some work experience in a Finance industry role will be viewed favorably.
·       Candidates with Economics, Accounting, Finance or Business degrees would be viewed favorably.
*PGIM welcomes all applicants, even if you don't meet every requirement. If your skills align with the role, we encourage you to apply.
What we offer you
• Private Medical Insurance: PGIM offers private medical insurance and pays the full premium on behalf of all employees.
• Annual Leave of 25 to 28 days, based on years of service, at full pay.
• Retirement Savings Plan: Employees receive a company contribution of 10% basic annual salary and a maximum employer-matching contribution of 5% of basic annual salary.
• Life Assurance & Income Protection: Life Assurance for 8 times your basic annual salary, up to a max benefit of £1.8million. 60% of your basic annual salary for a limited payment terms of 5 years, at the end of which a capital sum of 2x your basic annual salary is payable.

Job Description:
Start date: September 2027
Location: Stevenage
Duration: 3 years
Application: We love your interest in joining Airbus! There is no limit on the number of positions you can apply for, however, please be aware that you can only progress in the selection process for one position at a time. We recommend reviewing all available opportunities and applying to those that best match your experience and aspirations.
Closing date for applications: 30th January 2027
Salary: A competitive starting salary of £18,000
37 hours per week // Up to 2 Flexi Days per month // 25 days holiday plus bank holidays // Pension // Plus many more flexible benefits!
​​About Us:
Airbus is Europe’s number one Defence and Space enterprise, so what better way to start your Craft Apprenticeship than with an industry leader.
Being a Propulsion Manufacturing Technician Craft Apprentice at Airbus means you will get to develop both Mechanical and Electrical skills within our programme. You will be immersed in a stimulating Manufacturing environment.
This apprenticeship offers a unique opportunity to launch your career in the fascinating world of space propulsion. As a Propulsion Manufacturing Technician Apprentice, you'll be part of a team that builds cutting-edge propulsion systems for satellites and spacecraft. You'll gain hands-on experience in a supportive and innovative environment, contributing to projects that push the boundaries of technology.
This programme is perfect for those with a passion for both mechanical and electrical precision, a knack for problem-solving, and a keen interest in seeing their work take flight. Join us in shaping the future of space exploration!)
What you will be doing
Year 1: You will study towards a Level 2 Engineering Operative ST0537 on the mechanical/electrical pathways, gaining both academic knowledge and practical experience.
Year 2: During the Apprenticeship you will have a unique opportunity to experience our Propulsion Production area of the business which will provide you with a comprehensive understanding of how a Satellite is manufactured at Airbus Defence & Space.
This includes working in small teams or on a one-to-one basis to manufacture Spacecraft Propulsion systems using the latest approved processes and advanced production techniques for Satellite manufacture.
Your key activities & responsibilities will be:
Mechanical Assembly
• Use of various different adhesives and bonding methods
• Use of hand measuring tools to meet tight tolerances
• Installation of various components to satellite structures
• Installation of various connector brackets
• Bonding of Heater Mats, Thermocouples and Thermostats to various surfaces
• Following process and tolerances to drawings on 3DX
Orbital Welding
• Use our state-of-the-art Orbital Welding Machines to weld together Propulsion Systems into sub-assemblies before welding the sub-assemblies together on the full Satellite Structure.
• Learn how to bend, shape and cut both Titanium and Stainless-Steel pipework to form the Propulsion System.
Electrical
• Learn various Electrical Techniques such as Crimping, Splicing, Soldering and Forming of Harnesses.
• Installation of Electrical Components such as Latch Valves, Pressure Transducers and Thrusters using End to End Harness Installation.
• Wire and route Harnesses for Heater Mats, Thermocouples and Thermostats
During the 2nd year of the apprenticeship, you will attend a week of Team Building Activities and Exercises at one of the Outward-Bound UK Sites. Split up into teams consisting of Apprentices of all levels from various Airbus Defence and Space sites, you will work as a team to complete daily activities such as Rock Climbing, Hiking, Abseiling, Canoeing and more
Year 3: You will be fully on-site, fine tuning your hand skills against the business skills matrix.
Requirements
• Funding Eligibility: Applicants must be aged 16–21* and cannot hold a Level 2 or higher qualification (e.g., NVQ, BTEC, HND, or Degree) in Engineering, Aerospace, or related technical fields. For more information, please consult Foundation Apprenticeships Criteria*
• Education: No strict formal entry requirements, though a Grade 3 (or equivalent) in GCSE Maths and English is desirable.
• Skills & Attributes: Strong communication, reliability, excellent work ethic, a can-do attitude, and the ability to follow technical instructions and work well independently or in a team.
• No prior experience required—full on-the-job training will be provided.
BOOST YOUR APPLICATION
We want to get to know you! Not just your grades or school background so, tell us on your cover letter:
• Why Airbus?
What is it about Airbus that makes you excited to start a career with us? Is it our aircraft, innovation, global impact, or something else? Let us know what interests you about our work and why we stand out to you.
• Why a hands-on apprenticeship?
Why do you want to learn by doing? We’d love to hear what draws you to practical, skills-based learning.
• Show your hands-on experience.
In your CV or cover letter, include any hands-on activities or hobbies where you've used practical skills. These could be things like:
• DIY projects
• Building and fixing things
• Doing make-up or beauty work
• Tinkering and Tech Projects
• Building models
• Baking or cooking
• Others
Show Us What You've Built!
We love seeing what you are passionate about. If you've worked on any hands-on projects—whether it's building, baking, fixing something —we'd be thrilled to see it!
Feel free to attach photos, documents, or a short video showcasing a project you're proud of. This isn't a requirement, but it’s a fantastic way to give us a glimpse of your practical skills. We can't wait to see your work!
Important Information:
Joint-Venture: This Job Request will be allocated to the projected Joint-Venture scope towards a leading European player in space.
GOVERNMENT FUNDING*: This role is delivered as a government-funded Level 2 Apprenticeship. For more information about the eligibility criteria, please check the link: Foundation apprenticeship
SECURITY CLEARANCE: You will be subject to a BPSS (Baseline Personnel Security Standard) check. You may also need to gain UK SC-level Security Clearance or Export Control, depending on the role.
RIGHT TO WORK IN THE UK: Candidates must have current legal authorisation to work in the United Kingdom. For more information, please check the Government Website. Our apprenticeship roles do not meet the minimum requirements set by UK Visas & Immigration to enable sponsorship of migrant workers.
AI Guidance: We know you might be thinking about using AI to help you in your application - before you do, please read our guidelines on the use of AI for recruitment at Airbus http://airbus.com/en/careers/use-of-ai.
Contact:
Please let us know if you need us to make any adjustments to allow you to access and participate fully in the recruitment process. If you wish to discuss this further, please contact via email…

Job Description:
About Us
Flui Technologies is a leading software solution provider to the energy and water sector, delivering innovative and scalable software infrastructure and services since 1990. Our solutions - MarketFlow, MeterFlow and DCC adapter - support market competition, smart metering, network flexibility and supplier integration across Energy Retail, Energy Networks and Water Retail, and are used to manage messaging for more than 35 million electricity and gas meter points, with millions of records processed per day.
As the utility sector evolves to meet the challenges of Net Zero, Smart Metering, Energy Code reform, Market-wide Half-Hourly Settlement, Demand-side Response and Embedded Generation, we combine deep industry knowledge with technical innovation to deliver robust, business-focused solutions backed by dedicated people and exceptional support. We are certified to ISO/IEC 27001:2022, reflecting our commitment to protecting data and managing risk.
The Role
The Head of Cloud Platform Engineering owns the operations and component-level architecture of Flui's AWS cloud estate - the infrastructure that underpins software processing critical market and metering data at national scale. This is a hands-on role: you will design, build and run cloud-native platforms combining AWS-native services with open-source components, and carry end-to-end accountability for how that estate performs, costs, and stands up to scrutiny.
Beyond architecture and operations, you will own FinOps and security for the cloud estate, and act as the accountable owner for its overall fitness for purpose - resilience, performance and scalability - as Flui's platforms scale to support a growing and increasingly complex utility market. You will work closely with the engineering leadership to ensure architecture decisions serve both the product roadmap and the operational realities of running critical infrastructure.
The role suits someone who wants to remain genuinely hands-on with design and build, while holding single-point accountability for how well the cloud estate is run, secured and paid for.
Job Responsibilities
The Head of Cloud Platform Engineering will report to the Technology Director and will be responsible for:
•
Owning the component-level architecture of Flui's AWS cloud estate, spanning AWS-native services and open-source/self-managed components (e.g. container orchestration, messaging, data stores, observability tooling).
•
Operating and continuously improving the platforms underpinning MarketFlow, MeterFlow and DCC adapter, with direct accountability for their resilience, performance and scalability at national-scale transaction volumes.
•
Designing and maintaining disaster recovery, high-availability and capacity plans appropriate to platforms supporting critical utility market infrastructure.
•
Owning FinOps for the cloud estate: cost visibility, forecasting, tagging and allocation, and driving measurable, ongoing cost optimisation without compromising reliability.
•
Owning cloud security posture: identity and access management, network security, encryption, vulnerability and patch management, and ensuring the estate operates in line with Flui's ISO/IEC 27001 ISMS and wider compliance obligations.
•
Defining and maintaining the non-functional standards ('fitness for purpose') that platforms must meet - resilience, performance, scalability and observability - and holding engineering teams to them through architecture review and guardrails.
•
Remaining hands-on: designing, building and, where appropriate, personally implementing infrastructure-as-code, CI/CD pipelines and platform tooling alongside the wider engineering team.
•
Owning operational rigor for the estate - incident management, on-call practice, root-cause analysis and continuous improvement of SRE practices.
•
Making and owning build-vs-buy and AWS-native-vs-open-source decisions, balancing cost, control, operability and vendor lock-in.
•
Managing key vendor and technical relationships, including AWS itself and providers of critical open-source or commercial platform tooling.
•
Partnering with the product/engineering leadership to ensure cloud architecture decisions support the product roadmap and time-to-market, and recruiting/developing a small, high-calibre platform engineering team as the estate grows.
•
Championing knowledge sharing and technical education across engineering - documenting architecture decisions and standards, running internal sessions on cloud and platform practice, and mentoring engineers and technical colleagues to raise the wider team's capability.
Essential Competencies and Experience
Business Acumen
•
Demonstrable experience owning cloud platforms supporting a regulated, high-availability or critical-infrastructure business.
•
Ability to balance technical excellence with commercial and operational reality - cost, risk, and delivery pace.
•
Understanding of the utility/energy sector's data and resilience expectations is an advantage.
Cloud Architecture & Platform Engineering
•
Deep, hands-on AWS expertise across compute, storage, networking, data and security services, ideally evidenced by current AWS certification(s).
•
Proven experience designing and operating cloud-native platforms that combine AWS-native services with open-source components (e.g. Kubernetes, Terraform, Kafka or equivalent messaging, Prometheus/Grafana or equivalent observability).
•
Track record of owning a FinOps practice and delivering demonstrable, sustained cloud cost savings.
•
Strong cloud security background - IAM, encryption, vulnerability management - and familiarity with compliance frameworks such as ISO/IEC 27001.
•
Experience defining and meeting non-functional requirements: high availability, disaster recovery, performance/load testing and scalability at production scale.
General
•
Strong infrastructure-as-code skills (Terraform, CloudFormation or CDK) and mature CI/CD practice.
•
Comfortable operating hands-on day to day while also owning strategy, standards and team development.
•
A track record of sharing knowledge and raising technical capability across a team or wider engineering community - through documentation, mentoring, or internal training.
•
Willingness to participate in on-call/incident response as needed for platforms supporting critical services.
Job Qualifications
•
A degree in Computer Science, Engineering or a related discipline is a bonus, or equivalent hands-on experience.
•
Current AWS certification(s) - e.g. Solutions Architect Professional, DevOps Engineer Professional or Security Specialty - highly desirable.
Your Personal Characteristics Will Include
•
A pragmatic engineer-leader: hands-on by instinct, comfortable balancing strategic ownership with keyboard time.

Security and cost-conscious by default, without losing sight of reliability and delivery speed.

Calm and structured under pressure, with a methodical approach to incident response.

•
Establish relationships (both technical and business) at every level with a small set of strategic, regionally important software companies, and develop and implement a strategy to integrate the NVIDIA platform into these company’s products.
•
Develop and maintain deep technical expertise in agentic AI systems, open models, data science applications, and GPU-accelerated computing. Serve as the trusted technical advisor, problem solver, and champion for the developers within the software companies you support, collaborating with cross-functional partners to drive adoption of NVIDIA technologies.

Accelerate critical software company workloads by demonstrating and integrating the NVIDIA software stack (tools, libraries, SDKs, open models, NIMs, and blueprints) into partner products, platforms, and pipelines.

Map and monitor the developer ecosystem to identify growth opportunities, collaborating with engineering, product management, and marketing to inform roadmaps and optimize partner adoption strategies.

Engage partner technical leaders to drive best-practice integrations and resolve technical challenges, using regular syncs to track adoption, surface new workflows, and channel critical field insights back to NVIDIA product teams.
•
Represent NVIDIA at industry and developer events
•
Communicate the business and commercial value of integrating the NVIDIA platform into software company’s products
What We Need to See
•
Bachelor’s or Master’s degree or equivalent experience in Computer Science, Engineering, or a related field.
•
A minimum of 8+ years of overall professional experience in the technology industry in software engineering, developer relations, technical partnerships, solutions architect, product management, including 5+ years of direct hands-on experience in engaging with Product and Engineering organizations at enterprise-scale software companies on strategic product integrations.
•
Proven experience leading, partnering, scaling developer programs at major technology companies, and working on product integration with vertical-specific technology platforms or horizontal business applications.
•
Significant technical depth in AI/ML, customization of open models, or creation of agentic systems and contributions to product integrations and software libraries.
•
Experience leading technical collaborations with engineering and product teams - including architectural design, code reviews, technical mentorship, and delivery of technical talks or workshops
•
Proven track record to structure and implement sophisticated technical engagements, negotiate requirements, prioritize issues, and collaborate with internal or external collaborators (across sales, legal, product or marketing teams as needed).
•
Skilled at distilling complex technical concepts for audiences from engineers to executives, with end-to-end experience in defining, integrating, building, and jointly marketing solutions with strategic ISV partners.
•
Ability to conceptualize and communicate the commercial impact of integration of NVIDIA’s platform
Ways to Stand Out from the Crowd
•
Hands-on experience building or optimizing AI solutions with software companies building vertical specific technology platforms or horizontal business applications.
•
Exceptional ability to distill complex technical concepts and articulate value propositions to audiences ranging from AI/ML Engineers to C-suite executives, with end-to-end experience defining, integrating, building, and bringing solutions to market with strategic ISV partners
•
Familiarity with advanced computing, AI, and/or GPU acceleration platforms including agentic systems that incorporate domain-adapted, open models.
•
Successful history of building and scaling developer communities and delivering impactful technical enablement programs.
•
Expertise in building frameworks to capture developer sentiment and market shifts, translating real-time ecosystem dynamics into actionable intelligence for industry strategy and product rationalization.

Job Description:
Technical Manager AI Consultancy
NEW GROUND WON’T BREAK ITSELF.
Every day our teams help people in businesses and communities to do what is right and achieve their goals.
We’re happy to talk flexible working and consider reduced hours and job shares, we’ll support you to balance your work and life.
A look into the role
Knowing you’re right for us
We’ve set ambitious growth targets for the firm, and we need the right people to help us achieve these. We’re looking for people who will bring ambition and drive to their role. In changing markets, we need to be able to work at pace and be adaptable to change and to be curious, asking questions of ourselves, each other and our clients to ensure we are delivering the services and quality we expect.
As a technical Manager in our AI consultancy team, you will turn AI ideas into working solutions. You will work closely with clients, listening to their problems and agreeing what to build, but you will spend much of your time hands-on: building proofs of concept (early trials of AI ideas), writing code and guiding the next steps towards a live service.
You will also coordinate technical delivery teams from partner companies and other Grant Thornton firms, either embedded in teams or in some cases, leading them. We expect you to use Claude Code, Claude and other AI tools every day to build faster and to a higher standard, and to check carefully everything they produce.
Key responsibilities
Building and running proofs of concept
• Build working proofs of concept quickly, writing code yourself and using AI coding tools such as Claude Code
• Agree with clients what a proof of concept must show and how success will be judged
• Test results honestly, and explain clearly what worked, what did not and what it means
• Demonstrate your work and present findings to client teams in plain English
Going beyond the proof of concept
• Have a clear view of the path to live: the steps from a working trial to a secure, supported service that people use every day
• Build, or guide the building of, solutions to a standard that can grow beyond the trial
• Apply DevSecOps (building security into how software is built, tested and released) in your own work and in the work you review
• Keep cloud running costs visible and under control, following FinOps practice (managing the cost of cloud services)
Working with partner and delivery teams
• Coordinate technical delivery teams from partner companies and other Grant Thornton firms, agreeing clear roles, standards and ways of working
• Review their code, designs and results, and give clear, constructive feedback
• Work as an equal partner or in some cases, lead colleagues in every location and organisation
• Keep work on track for scope, timing, quality and budget, and raise risks early
Working with clients
• Run interviews and workshops with client teams to understand their problems, their data and how ready they are for AI
• Turn what you hear into clear technical options and sensible recommendations
• Explain technical choices simply to non-technical audiences
• Support senior colleagues with proposals, pitches and follow-up conversations
Producing high-quality work with AI tools
• Use Claude Code, Claude, Claude Design, Claude Cowork and other tools to write code, tests, documents, diagrams and client materials
• Check all AI-assisted work carefully for accuracy, security and quality before it reaches a client
• Share good practice, prompts and reusable code with the wider team
Responsible AI and risk
• Make sure solutions follow responsible AI principles, data protection law (including the UK General Data Protection Regulation, or UK GDPR) and sensible checks on how AI models are used and monitored
• Use only firm-approved tools when working with client information, and follow firm and client rules on how data is handled
• Keep code, client data and access details secure at all times
Joining us as a Technical Manager, the minimum criteria you’ll need is a degree in a technical subject, or equivalent professional experience and experience in building technology or AI solutions. It would be great if you had some of the following skills, but don’t worry if you don’t tick every box, we’ll help you develop along the way.
Essential
• Proven experience in building technology or AI solutions, in a consulting, technology or similar client-facing setting
• Hands-on coding skills, for example in Python, and experience building working prototypes quickly
• Regular, practical use of AI coding tools such as Claude Code to write, test and review code
• A good understanding of how large language models (the technology behind tools such as Claude) work, what they can and cannot do, and how to build useful solutions with them, for example by connecting them to a client’s own information
• Working knowledge of at least one major cloud provider (Microsoft Azure, Amazon Web Services or Google Cloud)
• A practical view of what it takes to move from proof of concept to live: testing, security, monitoring, support and cost
• An understanding of DevSecOps and FinOps principles
• Experience working with, or coordinating, technical teams in other organisations or locations
• Strong problem-solving skills, and the ability to explain technical ideas simply to non-technical people
• Good client skills, including listening, asking the right questions and building trust
Desirable
• Hands-on experience with AI-assisted building tools such as Cursor and Lovable
• Experience with AI agents (AI that can carry out tasks with limited supervision) and with connecting them to company systems
• Experience setting up automated testing and release processes
• Familiarity with data platforms and data governance
• Knowledge of AI regulation and responsible AI frameworks
• Experience with clients in financial services, private equity, the public sector or the mid-market
• Experience supporting bids and proposals
Tools
You will be expected to work confidently with Claude Code and other AI coding tools as we bring them into the team, alongside Claude, Claude Design, Claude Cowork and the Microsoft 365 suite. Experience with tools such as Cursor and Lovable is useful. Which tools you can use on client work depends on firm…

Incident and Problem Manager
About the Role
Capital One is searching for an Incident and Problem Manager to join our UK Technology Operations Centre (TOC) team. The TOC is dedicated to the effective management, coordination, and communication of all major and critical incidents, as well as owning post-incident Root Cause Analysis.
This role is highly service-focused and requires close liaison with internal Technology teams, Business Partners, and real-time engagement with sourcing partners and suppliers to effectively manage major and critical Incidents and Problems impacting our business.
Initiatives such as Reliability Testing Game Days utilising Chaos experiments to maintain always-on Incident readiness across UK Tech in our operational and technical response will be a prominent feature of this role so relevant experience in these areas is preferable.
The successful candidate must have strong Incident Management experience, a Technology background and experience in utilising AI to remove TOIL and add value. Exceptional communication skills and the ability to display a flexible problem solving approach are essential.
The TOC is a 24*7*365 operation with online presence between 08:00-17:30 and on-call coverage providing out of hours support.
What you’ll do
• Lead Investigations: You will direct investigations into major and critical incidents by managing, coordinating, and appropriately challenging technical resources on a 24*7*365 basis.
• Drive Communications: Ensure that incident progress is continuously tracked via action plans and communicated effectively to the wider organisation.
• Coordinate Teams for Quick Resolution: Lead virtual and office-based support teams to ensure the restoration of normal service operations as rapidly as possible, keeping business disruption to a minimum.
• Rigorous Root Cause Analysis: Conduct investigations into root cause utilising 5 why’s methodology, while establishing actions to prevent recurrence and raise standards across Tech.
• Drive Incident Readiness: Greater service stability means fewer opportunities to prove tech resiliency and sharpen critical Incident behaviours. You’ll play a key role ensuring our people and Tech are always ready via Game Days in support of our Reliability Assurance agenda.
• Spearhead Process Improvement: Lead process and service improvement initiatives that align with your personal development objectives. This is your chance to embrace AI, as well as automate repetitive, manual incident and problem management tasks.
• Provide On-Call Support: You will perform on-call cover for Incident Management on rotation.
What we’re looking for
• An inquisitive and proactive mindset.
• Ability to communicate openly and effectively in both written and verbal form, with the confidence to meet effectively with external and internal Senior stakeholders.
• The ability to remain calm and focused in a pressured environment, carefully considering the needs of multiple stakeholders.
• An understanding of AWS Cloud technology principles. (Note: If you have advanced technical skills here, you will be highly empowered to drive automation!)
• Highly organised with an ability to remain focused and flexible when managing multiple initiatives
• Prior experience of using AI to drive process improvement initiatives that have added tangible value
Where and how you'll work
This is a permanent position and is based in our Nottingham Head Office.
We have a hybrid working model which gives you flexibility to work from our offices and from home.
We’re big on collaboration and connection, so you’ll be based in our office 3 days a week on Tuesdays, Wednesdays and Thursdays.
What’s in it for you
• Bring us all this - and you’ll be handsomely rewarded with a role contributing to the product roadmap for an organisation committed to transformation
• We’re continuing our journey into the public cloud and have problems of scale, security, availability and performance for you to help solve
• We offer high performers strong and diverse career progression, investing heavily in developing great people through our Capital One University training programmes (and appropriate external providers)
• Immediate access to our core benefits including pension scheme, bonus, generous holiday entitlement and private medical insurance – with flexible benefits available including season-ticket loans, cycle to work scheme and enhanced parental leave
• Open-plan workspaces and facilities designed to inspire and support you. In London, you can heighten your mood with a run on our rooftop running track or an espresso at the Workshop Coffee café

We want to work with top talent: whoever you are, whatever you look like, wherever you come from. We know it’s about what you do, not just what you say. That’s why we make our recruitment process fair and accessible. And we offer benefits that attract people at all ages and stages.
We also partner with organisations including the Women in Finance and Race At Work Charters, Stonewall and upReach to find people from every walk of life and help them thrive with us. We have a whole host of internal networks and support groups you could be involved in, to name a few:

The International Rescue Committee (IRC) responds to the world's worst humanitarian crises, helping to restore health, safety, education, economic wellbeing, and power to people devastated by conflict and disaster. Founded in 1933 at the call of Albert Einstein, the IRC is one of the world's largest international humanitarian non-governmental organizations (INGO), at work in more than 40 countries and 29 U.S. cities helping people to survive, reclaim control of their future and strengthen their communities. Background of the project
The International Rescue Committee (IRC) engages a rapidly growing pool of cost-evidence-based funders, whose allocation decisions are primarily based on rigorous impact-per-dollar analysis. Historically, humanitarian programming has not been a focus of this funder community. However, in recent years, the IRC has increasingly received cost-evidence-based funder support for a wide range of initiatives, from conducting exploratory research to scaling malnutrition treatment to influencing foreign aid. As the “Solutions NGO”, cost-evidence-based funders represent a values- and results-aligned opportunity to increase the reach and cost-effectiveness of IRC’s programming.
This consultancy sits within the Best Use of Resources (BUR) team and reports to the Senior Director, Cost-effectiveness. It is a time-limited engagement to support IRC’s relationships, value proposition and funding from cost-evidence-based funders, and to strengthen the BUR team’s own capability in the analysis these funders expect.
Scope of work
Working with the Senior Director, Cost-effectiveness, and in deep collaboration with other IRC colleagues, the Consultant will produce materials that deepen and grow a portfolio of cost-evidence-based funder relationships, translate BUR’s cost-effectiveness research and IRC’s programming into donor-facing funding opportunities, and build IRC’s thought leadership profile within the community.
In consultation with the Senior Director, Cost-effectiveness, the Consultant will determine the method and means of performing the work. The content of each deliverable will be agreed in advance with the Senior Director, Cost-effectiveness, who will review and accept deliverables.

Are you an RF & Electronics Engineer looking for a new challenge in a production-facing design support role? Do you enjoy problem solving and collaboration where no two days are the same? Our team of Production Support Engineers is expanding and we are looking for a motivated & experienced individual to undertake a production support lead role focused on transceiver-based datalink products that are used within industry leading missile systems.
Salary: £54-61K depending on experience
Dynamic (hybrid) working: 4-5 days per week on-site due to workload classification
Security Clearance: British Citizen or a Dual UK national with British citizenship
Restrictions and/or limitations relating to nationality and/or rights to work may apply. As a minimum and after offer stage, all successful candidates will need to undergo HMG Basic Personnel Security Standard checks (BPSS), which are managed by the MBDA Personnel Security Team.
What we can offer you:
• Company bonus: Up to £2,500 (based on company performance and will vary year to year
• Pension: maximum total (employer and employee) contribution of up to 14%
• Overtime: opportunity for paid overtime
• Flexi Leave: Up to 15 additional days
• Flexible working: We welcome applicants who are looking for flexible working arrangements
• Enhanced parental leave: offers up to 26 weeks for maternity, adoption and shared parental leave -enhancements are available for paternity leave, neonatal leave and fertility testing and treatments
• Facilities: Fantastic site facilities including subsidised meals, free car parking and much more…
The opportunity:
We have a fantastic opportunity for an RF & Electronics Engineer to play a leading role in the support of Datalink production activities at our state of the art manufacturing facility in Bolton.
Reporting to the Production Design Support delivery team leader, as the appointed Production Support Lead for our Datalink products in Bolton you will mainly interface between the Design Authority in Stevenage and the various Manufacturing teams in Bolton working on products in series production and under development. As a highly motivated, driven & experienced engineer you will be required to respond to any issues raised by Manufacturing and/or Design teams that may affect our ability to deliver product with a strong emphasis on raising & maintaining high yield rates.
You will be expected to demonstrate hands-on, face to face production support in many forms such as devising and conducting factory-based trials & proving activities, generating formal evidence and effective collaboration with various Engineering & Operations Managers, Quality Assurance, Supply Chain & Design Authorities when resolving unforeseen production issues. You will be required to generate an in-depth understanding our Datalink Products & associated Test Equipment designs including production test requirements in order to quickly & effectively distinguish the correct root cause of the issue(s) and the subsequent resolution process. You will also be required to act as a key stakeholder & peer reviewer for new, emerging Datalink designs focusing on providing feedback in relation to Design for Test and Design for Manufacture based upon experience & problems raised by Manufacturing.
In addition, you will be required to provide RF technical leadership & guidance to other support engineers in the team. Drawing on your experiences you will work autonomously in isolation or within small, focused investigation teams who will be looking to you for guidance and support in relation to RF components, circuits, systems, testing & analysis. Where minor revisions to product designs are required, you will act as the main contact interfacing between the Design Authority and Manufacturing, fulfilling and overseeing any practical evidence gathering activities including the generation of requirement documentation.
The role offers the successful candidate a true engineering challenge in their core discipline(s), whilst providing scope for personal growth and development in other areas of electronics while working on some of the most exciting missile & platform programmes in defence.
Working within Production Design support team is a challenging but highly rewarding role as you not only see designs coming to life in the manufacturing environment but you can help to shape the design of these products to deliver support to our customers.
What we're looking for from you:
• Proven practical RF design, testing & Fault Finding of RF circuits down to component level across a wide frequency range including Low Noise Amplifiers (LNA’s), High Power Amplifiers (HPA’s), filters & attenuators, local oscillators, synthesisers, modulator design etc.
• Experience using RF design tools ( eg Microwave Office), including layout.
• Significant RF Test & Measurement experience including fault finding, RF calibration and measurement uncertainty is highly desirable and the proficient use of RF test equipment including Vector Network Analysers (VNA’s), Spectrum Analysers, Oscilloscopes & Power Meters etc.
• Experience in RF production test requirements and evaluation of correct implementation via test equipment
• Excellent practical skills including soldering, designing and building development boards for proving activities etc.
• Good knowledge of digital, analogue and power supply design
• Fully conversant with manufacturing techniques and capabilities, including design for manufacture and test.
• Strong communicator with excellent presentation and report writing skills. Able to communicate clearly any problems, solutions or results to various teams at all levels including Design Authorities, customers & Suppliers. Able to provide demonstrations and training to other support engineers.

The Team:
The ESG Data Owner role sits within the Data Enablement team at S&P Dow Jones Indices. The team supports the management, validation, and delivery of datasets used in the maintenance and rebalance of S&P Dow Jones indices across multiple asset classes.
This role will focus on ESG data used in equity and fixed income indices, including datasets such as GHG emissions, physical risk, ESG scores, and related sustainability data. You will help ensure these datasets are accurate, well-documented, and ready for use by internal stakeholders.
You will work closely with technical, operational, and index teams to support reliable data delivery, improve data quality checks, and maintain clear data governance practices, including documentation, lineage, controls, and issue resolution.
Responsibilities and Impact
As an ESG Data Owner, you will play a central role in the day-to-day management, quality, and governance of ESG data used across S&P Dow Jones equity and fixed income indices. You will help ensure ESG datasets are complete, accurate, timely, and fit for use in index operations and analytics.
This role acts as a key point of coordination between data operations, technology, index management, analytics, and vendor teams. You will support the onboarding of new datasets, help define data requirements, monitor data quality, investigate issues, and contribute to improvements in ESG data processes and controls.
Key Responsibilities
• Manage ESG datasets across the data lifecycle, including ingestion, validation, quality review, documentation, and delivery for index use.
• Support the preparation and maintenance of ESG datasets such as GHG emissions, physical risk, ESG scores, and other sustainability-related data.
• Apply data standards, taxonomies, and governance controls to help maintain a consistent and trusted version of ESG data across index and analytics workflows.
• Design, run, and improve data quality checks to identify gaps, inconsistencies, outliers, and other data issues.
• Investigate and resolve data quality issues in collaboration with technology, operations, index management, and vendor teams.
• Help define data requirements for new or updated ESG data feeds, including field definitions, validation rules, lineage requirements, and operational handoff needs.
• Support the onboarding of new ESG datasets and help ensure they are integrated into existing systems and processes in a controlled and documented way.
• Maintain clear documentation of data sources, business rules, validation checks, known limitations, and data lineage.
• Act as a point of contact for internal ESG data questions, working with index managers and other teams to clarify data usage, resolve queries, and support methodology alignment.
• For complex data cases, prepare analysis and recommendations to support review by index managers, committees, or relevant internal stakeholders.
• Coordinate with ESG data vendors to clarify data definitions, delivery standards, issue resolution, and data changes.
• Stay informed on ESG market developments, data standards, and regulatory themes that may affect ESG data requirements.
• Prepare data analysis summaries, issue logs, and reporting materials to support internal reviews and stakeholder discussions.
• Support responses to client or stakeholder questions by providing accurate ESG data information through internal teams such as Client Services or Index Services.
What is in it for you?
• Opportunity to work in the financial data and index industry with a focus on ESG and sustainability data.
• Exposure to ESG datasets used across equity and fixed income indices.
• Opportunity to work with data management, index, analytics, sustainability, technology, and operations teams.
• Development of practical skills in data quality, data governance, validation, documentation, and pipeline support.
• Access to data management tools, analytical methods, and cross-asset index concepts.
What We’re Looking For:
Basic Required Qualifications:
• Bachelor's degree in Data Science, Finance, Economics, Mathematics, or a related field.
• 1–3 years of professional experience in data analysis, data management, ESG data, sustainability, indexing, or a similar financial or data-driven field.
• A foundational understanding of ESG frameworks, ratings methodologies, and sustainability data (e.g., GHG emissions, physical risk, ESG scores) and their application in financial indices.
• A foundational understanding of financial markets (equity & fixed income) and indexing concepts.
• Strong analytical and quantitative skills with the ability to work with large data sets.
• Proficiency in Python and SQL for data analysis, manipulation, and visualization with a willingness to further develop these skills in a financial data environment.
• Good written and verbal communication skills with the ability to explain complex topics clearly.
• Strong attention to detail and ability to manage multiple priorities and deadlines in a structured, process-driven environment.
• Ability to work collaboratively in a fast-paced, global environment.
Preferred Qualifications:
• Awareness of ESG-related regulatory frameworks (e.g., EU Taxonomy, SFDR, TCFD) and their implications for index construction and data requirements.
• Familiarity with ESG data providers (e.g., S&P Global Sustainable1, Sustainalytics, CDP, SBTi).
• Experience in project management and implementing process improvements.
• Exposure to data governance frameworks, data lineage concepts, or master data management practices.
• Experience with data visualization tools (e.g., Tableau, Power BI) or cloud-based data platforms (Databricks).

At S&P Dow Jones Indices, we provide iconic and innovative index solutions backed by unparalleled expertise across the asset-class spectrum. By bringing transparency to the global capital markets, we empower investors everywhere to make decisions with conviction. We’re the largest global resource for index-based concepts, data and research, and home to iconic financial market indicators, such as the S&P 500® and the Dow Jones Industrial Average®. Job Title: Procurement Excellence Lead
Location: UK - London preferred (Hybrid)
Reports to: Group Head of Procurement
About the role
We are looking for a Procurement Excellence Lead to help shape how BSI's Group Procurement function operates as it continues its transformation.
Acting as a senior partner to the Group Head of Procurement, you will own the execution side of the procurement operating model - bringing consistency to ways of working, governance, digital enablement, templates, Supplier Relationship Management and the operational delivery of sustainable procurement and Scope 3 priorities.
This role is about making procurement easier to execute well: creating practical standards, tools and controls that are scalable, auditable and proportionate, while helping the function build confidence, capability and stronger day-to-day delivery.
Key Responsibilities
• Own and continually improve end-to-end procurement ways of working across Source-to-Contract and Supplier Management.
• Translate procurement policy and strategy into practical guidance, clear roles, decision points and minimum standards that teams can apply consistently.
• Ensure procurement processes are proportionate to value and risk while supporting defensible decision-making, audit readiness and regulatory compliance.
• Act as business owner for procurement enablement and tooling, shaping requirements and driving adoption of eSourcing, SRM, CLM and related digital solutions.
• Own the procurement template and toolkit library, including RFx packs, pricing schedules, evaluation models, moderation packs and award documentation.
• Drive consistent use of standard sourcing approaches and act as a centre of expertise for complex or high-risk procurement activity.
• Lead the governance framework for Supplier Relationship Management, including supplier segmentation, governance cadence, scorecards and escalation pathways.
• Lead the operational enablement of Procurement's Scope 3 strategy, embedding sustainability considerations into sourcing, supplier engagement and SRM.
• Work closely with Sustainability, Finance, Risk, Legal, Internal Audit, IT and Transformation teams to align governance, data and control requirements.
• Define and track management information that demonstrates adoption, quality and maturity across procurement ways of working.
• Support the Group Head of Procurement with senior stakeholder, audit and governance materials and with the operational delivery of the procurement transformation roadmap.
What we're looking for
• Extensive experience in procurement, procurement transformation or procurement operating model design.
• Strong understanding of Source-to-Contract, procurement governance, supplier management and audit requirements.
• Proven ability to design and embed standard ways of working, templates and toolkits at scale.
• Experience supporting or leading procurement digital enablement, including eSourcing, SRM, CLM or comparable platforms.
• Experience enabling sustainable procurement or Scope 3 objectives through procurement processes and supplier engagement.
• Strong strategic thinking with the ability to translate strategy and policy into practical execution.
• Excellent stakeholder management and influencing skills, with the credibility to operate at senior leadership level.
• Clear communication skills and the ability to simplify complex requirements into usable guidance.
• Relevant degree or equivalent professional experience.
Highly desirable
• Experience building procurement capability or learning frameworks.
• Experience operating in regulated, audit-focused or otherwise complex organisational environments.
• Continuous improvement, change or transformation experience.
BSI offers a competitive total reward package in an independent and varied Global environment, flexible working hours, ongoing training and development with the inclusion of 27-days annual leave, paid sick leave, bank holidays, health insurance, life insurance, pension plan with company contribution, car allowance (dependent on role), income protection, paid maternity leave, paid paternity leave, paid parental leave, adoption leave, compassionate leave, paid bereavement leave, learning and development opportunities, and a wide range of flexible benefits that you can tailor to suit your lifestyle.
Do you believe the world deserves excellence?
Headquartered in London, BSI is the world's first national standards organization with more than 100 years of experience. We are a global partner for 86,000 companies and organizations in over 193 countries, offering development, auditing, certification, and training services, including innovative software solutions and cyber security expertise for all industries: from aerospace and automotive to food, construction, energy, healthcare, IT and trade sectors. Incorporated by Royal Charter, we’re truly impartial, and home to the ultimate mark of trust, the Kitemark.
Through our unique combination of consulting, training, assurance and regulatory services we bring solid and broad knowledge to every company.
If you want to contribute to this inspiring challenge, bring your open and enthusiastic mindset to our dynamic team, apply now and become part of the BSI family!

BSI is committed to ensuring the diversity of our workforce reflects that of our clients and the communities in which we operate. Our goal is to create a sense of belonging for all employees by providing opportunities to develop, grow, and engage with our global organization all while having fun doing great work. BSI is a community where everyone can thrive.

vantagedc.wd1.myworkdayjobs.com/vantage/.description_excerpt:
About Vantage
Vantage powers, cools, protects and connects the technology of the world’s well-known hyperscalers, cloud providers and large enterprises. Developing and operating across North America, EMEA and Asia Pacific, Vantage has evolved data center design in innovative ways to deliver dramatic gains in reliability, efficiency and sustainability in flexible environments that can scale as quickly as the market demands.
Product Department
The Product team at Vantage defines and stewards our global product platform: the customer outcomes we aim to deliver, the standards and reference approaches that make delivery repeatable, and the closed-loop learning that turns each deployment into an upgrade for the next. We do this in partnership with Engineering, Delivery, Operations, Procurement, Sustainability, Sales, Site Selection, and Business Development, aligning priorities and trade-offs while preserving clear functional ownership for design execution, construction delivery, and site operations.
Position Overview
Vantage is building a repeatable, product-led approach to delivering hyperscale infrastructure and operating data centers on a global scale. We are hiring a Senior Manager, Product Performance Benchmarking to establish and evolve the product performance benchmarking capability at the heart of that approach. The benchmarking engine is the governed reference for our products across the full lifecycle, regions, and customer configurations, and will sit behind pricing, RFP responses, and executive reporting for a growing global portfolio.
It evaluates the expected schedule, cost, and sustainability of our products across design, delivery, and operations: how long they should take to build, and what they should cost to build and to run.
This is a senior individual contributor role expected to grow into team leadership for someone who combines deep benchmarking, estimating, preconstruction, and project controls experience with the commercial judgement to lead methodology, challenge conventions, and turn data into decisions. You will define what the benchmark should answer, how it is governed, how it is used in decisions, and how internal and external inputs become a durable capability.
What You Will Own
You will build the product performance intelligence capability behind Vantage’s global data center platform. This is not a reporting role. It is a chance to define how one of the fastest-scaling infrastructure companies measures cost, schedule, sustainability, lifecycle performance, and value realization across regions, product configurations, and customer requirements.
The benchmark you build will shape real decisions: how products are configured, how products translate into cost, schedule, and sustainability impacts, how trade-offs are made, where performance is improving, and where the business needs to change. You will work at the intersection of Product, Engineering, Delivery, Operations, Procurement, Sustainability, and Analytics, with visibility to senior leaders and direct influence over how Vantage becomes more repeatable, data-driven, and product-led.
What You Will Do
•
Define the governed benchmarking methodology, baseline assumptions, performance measures, and usage rules Vantage applies globally to configure, cost, schedule, approve, manage, and measure project performance across Product, Engineering, Delivery, Operations, and Sustainability.
•
Own the benchmark roadmap across platform, product, regional baselines, configurations, and future product extensions.
•
Translate Product, Procurement, Preconstruction, Project Controls, and Sustainability requirements into benchmark scope.
•
Lead consultant engagement, reviewing methodology, assumptions, confidence bands, and deliverables.
•
Own the WBS/CBS and schedule structure from a product, business-adoption, and use perspective.
•
Govern baseline, regional variant, configuration bridge, and factor-pack logic.
•
Partner with key stakeholders to incorporate market intelligence, supplier input, and realized cost factors into benchmark updates where appropriate.
•
Define target audiences, provide business interpretation, and set reporting requirements for benchmark outputs to senior stakeholders, while partnering with analytics roles on dashboard build and data automation.
•
Decide when benchmark outputs are fit for use in RFPs, ROM business cases, customer discussions, product decisions, and executive reporting.
•
Own what decisions the benchmark enables and state clearly where confidence is insufficient.
What Success Looks Like
•
A governed product performance benchmark model exists that connects capital cost, schedule, sustainability and operational cost (energy, efficiency, maintainability) into a single governed reference with explicit methodology, confidence bands, and stated limits.
•
Standardized KPIs and performance criteria are set, with the ability to reliably compare projects across approved variants, regions, and product versions from pre-construction through operations.
•
Benchmark outputs are used in real decisions — RFPs, ROM business cases, customer discussions, product trade-offs, and executive reporting — under clear fitness-for-use rules.
•
The WBS/CBS and schedule structures are adopted by Product, Procurement, Preconstruction, Project Controls, and Sustainability, and held under company change control.
•
Baseline, regional variant, configuration bridge, and factor-pack logic is coherent and current, with refresh cycles running on a disciplined cadence.
•
Benchmarking exists as a durable internal capability that gets better with data from each delivery project. Results inform enhancements to products, variants, and project delivery to continuously improve.
•
Methodology, models, and refresh are owned in-house, with external inputs from consultants, market data, and suppliers integrated deliberately rather than relied upon by default.
•
Senior stakeholders receive interpretation, not just numbers: what moved, why, and what decision it supports.
What We Are Looking For
•
Benchmarking and cost intelligence: 8–12 years in cost management, quantity surveying, preconstruction, owner’s representative, project controls, infrastructure benchmarking, or equivalent capital-project performance role. Exceptional candidates with fewer years of experience may be considered.
•
Capital project modeling: Demonstrated experience building or governing cost, schedule, or TCO models for complex capital programs, including unit rates, quantities, escalation, regional factors, configuration deltas, and confidence ranges.
•
Lifecycle performance orientation: Ability to connect capital cost, schedule, energy, operational cost, maintainability, and sustainability factors into a decision-ready view of product performance.
•
Continuous learning: Experience comparing benchmarks to actual delivery outcomes and translating variance into actionable recommendations for design, procurement, delivery, or product roadmap…

springernature.wd3.myworkdayjobs.com/spr.description_excerpt:
Purpose of the role
The way that academic research is being communicated to audiences around the globe is changing rapidly. Increasingly, research data can be consumed at scale through AI tools and machine intelligence, creating a moment of transition in research communication, and an opportunity to shape how millions discover, trust, and apply research, accelerating the translation of insight into real‑world impact faster than before.
The purpose of this role is to turn Springer Nature’s traffic, usage and discovery data into the signals and evidence the team relies on to maximise the value of our content across the web, navigating this transition. This role sits at the intersection of content discoverability, content protection and data intelligence.
You will help the organisation understand how Springer Nature content is being discovered, accessed and used across search engines, academic discovery services, AI-powered tools, content aggregation platforms and other external channels. At the same time, you will identify and measure inappropriate access, automated scraping and content extraction activities to ensure discoverability is achieved without undermining platform traffic, entitlements or commercial value.
You will own the analytical foundations of both disciplines: identifying and measuring the signals that indicate successful discovery, as well as those that indicate abuse. Working closely with product, platform, analytics and security teams, you will provide the evidence needed to shape strategy, prioritise interventions and measure outcomes.
Key Responsibilities
Content Discoverability & External Platform Analytics
• Analyse how Springer Nature content is discovered across external channels, including search engines, scholarly discovery services, library platforms, aggregators, citation networks, AI-powered discovery tools and emerging content platforms
• Develop and maintain a framework of discoverability metrics, signals and KPIs to measure the effectiveness of content distribution and discovery strategies
• Identify the external signals that indicate successful content discovery, engagement and conversion back to Springer Nature properties
• Measure the impact of metadata quality, indexing, platform integrations and content syndication on discoverability outcomes
• Track changes in referral patterns, search visibility and external platform behaviour, identifying opportunities and risks
• Evaluate the trade-offs between maximising reach and preserving platform traffic, user engagement and commercial value
• Provide recommendations to product and business stakeholders on how content should be surfaced, exposed and protected across external ecosystems
• Build analytical models to understand the relationship between discoverability, content consumption, platform traffic and downstream business outcomes
Content Protection & Traffic Intelligence
• Analyse WAF, traffic and behavioural data, primarily in BigQuery, to identify scraping, bot activity and unauthorised content extraction using fingerprint analysis, behavioural signals and network data
• Build and maintain a portfolio of detection signals and continuously evolve them as threat actors change their tactics
• Measure detection performance through coverage, precision, false-positive rates and baseline benchmarking
• Quantify the scale and commercial impact of content scraping and content leakage to support prioritisation and investment decisions
• Investigate incidents and anomalous traffic patterns, distinguishing legitimate institutional and authenticated users from malicious automation
• Work closely with the Security Specialist Engineer, who will implement and enforce controls, while you identify, measure and validate the underlying signals
• Help define the evidence base for decisions about content exposure, rate limiting, entitlement enforcement and platform protections
Insight, Reporting & Stakeholder Engagement
• Design and maintain dashboards and reporting that communicate discoverability performance, content protection effectiveness and emerging risks
• Translate complex data findings into clear recommendations for product, platform, security and senior stakeholders
• Establish meaningful baselines, benchmarks and success measures for both discoverability and protection initiatives
• Support product strategy by providing evidence-driven insights into user behaviour, content consumption patterns and external ecosystem trends
• Contribute to experimentation and measurement frameworks that assess the impact of product, metadata, discovery and protection changes
Essential Skills & Experience
• Strong SQL skills, particularly BigQuery, with experience working on large-scale datasets.
• Strong analytical and statistical capability, including the ability to identify patterns, anomalies and behavioural trends
• Experience analysing web traffic, referral data and user journeys across digital products.
• Understanding of content discoverability, search and referral ecosystems, or the ability to quickly develop expertise in this area
• Interest in bot detection, behavioural analytics, fingerprinting and content protection challenges
• Ability to connect multiple data sources to build a coherent picture of user behaviour and content usage
• Excellent communication skills, with the ability to turn data insights into actionable recommendations and compelling stakeholder narratives
• Strong understanding of data security and governance
Desirable
• Python or other scripting experience for data analysis and automation
• Experience with dashboarding and visualisation platforms such as Looker, Grafana or similar tools
• Exposure to security analytics, threat intelligence or fraud detection
• Understanding of SEO, scholarly discovery services, content metadata or digital content distribution ecosystems
• Familiarity with access management, authentication or entitlement systems
• Experience within academic publishing, research information systems or scholarly communications
• Experience with modern data transformation tooling such as Dataform or dbt
• Experience developing classification or machine learning models for user behaviour analysis, anomaly detection or segmentation
• Experience measuring the impact of external platforms on traffic, engagement, discoverability and commercial outcomes

Role summary
The Financial Crime and Sanctions Analyst is a junior-level, second-line role in the Financial Crime and Sanctions (FCS) Team, part of the firm's Legal Department. The role supports the day-to-day implementation of the firm's financial crime and sanctions controls, with a particular focus on client due diligence and reverifications, ongoing monitoring of clients and matters, sanctions monitoring, and gifts and hospitality, as well as support for the firm's remediation project.
You will be at the forefront of compliance in a fast-paced, global environment and will have the opportunity to work on challenging and engaging matters. The focus of this role will be analysing the financial crime, sanctions and reputational risks of existing clients, identifying and gathering client due diligence materials, and escalating key issues to more senior members of the FCS Team.
The role will also involve supporting the FCS Team with quality control (including recording data and analysing trends), regulatory reporting, internal and regulatory audits, and other risk management and compliance projects, such as the implementation of new systems and tools.
Location Overview: Manchester
The Freshfields Global Centre provides both business and legal services to the firm. Our services are delivered in a way which supports the global nature of our firm and our clients, enables our fee earners to deliver exceptional service to our clients and to do that in a way which is efficient and effective.
Function Overview: Legal Department
This department, made up of both qualified lawyers and non-lawyers, exists to manage the firm's risk exposure and to provide advice to the partners on a range of legal and compliance issues. The Financial Crime and Sanctions Analyst will be a member of the global Financial Crime and Sanctions (FCS) Team in the Legal Department. The FCS Team provides advice to the firm on compliance with financial crime and sanctions legislation and gives guidance on reputational risk matters.
Key responsibilities and deliverables
1) Client reverifications and backlog reduction (AML compliance)
• Facilitating the ongoing monitoring process in coordination with partners and fee earners, particularly in the collection and analysis of due diligence material and records for client reverification purposes.
• Driving down the existing client reverification backlog by working through outstanding reverifications in line with agreed priorities and timescales, and tracking and reporting progress to the FCS Team.
2) Ongoing monitoring of clients and matters (AML compliance)
• Providing support and assistance to the FCS Team principally on client due diligence matters.
• Reviewing records, conducting research, screening for PEPs, sanctions, and adverse media, and reputational risk analysis for existing clients with a view to keeping documentation and information for client risk assessments up-to-date and to agreed standards appropriate for review by internal and external stakeholders such as internal audit and regulators.
• Supporting the ongoing monitoring of high-risk clients and matters in coordination with partners and fee earners, including checking that enhanced due diligence and clearance conditions have been applied and documented, and escalating any new or increased financial crime risks to more senior members of the FCS Team.
3) Sanctions monitoring (sanctions compliance)

Security Clearance
At Leonardo, many of our roles are subject to security and export control restrictions set by UK Government Security requirements and customer obligations.  As a result, and in line with the UK Government Baseline Personnel Security Standard (BPSS) requirements, all successful applicants will be asked to provide evidence of identity, eligibility to work in the UK, criminal record declaration information and employment and/or education history verification for the previous five years.
For staff operating in more sensitive posts, there is an additional range of personnel security controls referred to as National Security Vetting (NSV).  As part of this process, a range of factors may be considered, including an individual's background, travel history, nationality, previous nationalities held and other information relevant to the vetting assessment.
To be eligible for National Security Vetting at SC level, applicants will generally be expected to have continuously resided in the UK for the previous five years. For DV clearance, this is typically ten years.  In some circumstances, time spent overseas may be accepted, with additional overseas checks.  Additional vetting requirements may apply upon appointment.

Job Description:
What you'll do as a Senior Stress Engineer:
Mechanical Engineering is a fundamental element of all our products.
Your role as a Senior Stress Engineer will be primarily to support product designs that are in-service or being developed for customers by providing the necessary structural verification that demonstrates compliance against customer and or regulatory specifications. You will communicate key aspects of results and findings to project integrated teams and the company airworthiness authority and technically advise on all aspects of stress engineering activities. It will involve working with multi-discipline project teams, interfacing with customers (internal and external) and liaising closely with engineers from many other disciplines.
Typically, you will:
• Assess mechanical designs for strength, durability (fatigue), performance and safety against regulatory and customer requirements through application of appropriate methodologies i.e. finite element techniques and/or classical hand calculations.
• Provide guidance on structural design improvements relating to component sustainability and manufacturing considerations.
• Provide recommendations on component or sub assembly optimisation i.e. mass reduction, reduced part count etc.
• Support the selection of manufacturing technologies and materials based on a sound understanding of mechanical engineering principles e.g. statics, dynamics (vibration and shock), strength of materials and failure mechanisms.
• Support all structural aspects of product development from concept design through to test and certification.
What we need from you:
• The candidate should have a degree in Mechanical or Aeronautical Engineering with post-graduate experience in stress & vibration engineering.
• Professional recognition as a Chartered Engineer or proven associated competencies is desirable.
• It is advantageous for the candidate to have experience in the design, development and test of electronics packaging and/or aerospace systems equipment.
• A proven knowledge of structural analysis and previous experience in developing equipment for extreme operating environments to RTCA DO160 and MIL-STD-810 mechanical requirements.
• The candidate will be competent in the use of Finite Element Analysis (FEA), preferably Siemens Simcenter & Nastran and be competent in the fundamentals of load balancing i.e. free-body diagrams and application of classical hand calculations using empirical methods in lieu of FEA or in validation of FEA results.
• Experience of environmental testing methods (shock, vibration, acceleration) and post-processing of test results for design verification is highly desirable.
• Verbal and written communication skills are essential in this role as there will be a high level of interaction with both internal and external customers.
• Capable of working unsupervised within a team environment.
Security Clearance
You must be eligible for full UK security clearance.  For more information and guidance please visit : https://www.gov.uk/government/publications/united-kingdom-security-vetting-clearance-levels
